name: Resume

claims.claim_text: Resume screening for engineering roles targets specific demonstrated experience rather than general capability: an EDA vendor hiring a board designer looks for prior use of that vendor's own tool and a large number of boards already designed.
claims.quote_verbatim: when people scan resumes, right? They're looking for experience. They're looking for expertise in a very specific field
claims.episode_title: Contests, Ham Radio & TWIT.tv - Ham, Spam, Thank You Ma'am

claims.claim_text: A self-published online record of personal projects supplements a conventional resume by showing what a candidate has done rather than only where they have been employed; unpaid technical work such as a university solar car team or home electronics is what stands out to a resume reviewer.
claims.quote_verbatim: kind of like the new resume, you know, you don't, it's not necessarily just showing where you've worked, but also what you've done

claims.claim_text: In the judgment of an engineer who screened resumes for hiring, academic journal publications count for little in practical industry, whereas articles in hobbyist electronics magazines such as Silicon Chip or Nuts and Volts are read as evidence of hands-on work.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I'm reading someone's resume and it says, oh, I've published these papers, and they're like, hey, I'm going to go, I don't give a shit
claims.episode_title: Magnets, China & IEEE - Xenomorphic Xerox Xebec
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Contributing to an existing open-source project supplies verifiable project experience to a candidate who has none from employment, including non-design roles such as project management.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a lot of open source projects out there. There's countless ones. Why didn't you do anything?

claims.claim_text: Some hiring practitioners ask candidates for photographs of boards they have designed instead of a resume as the first point of contact.
claims.quote_verbatim: don't send me your resume. Send me pictures of boards you've designed.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr Greg Charvat - Watcher of Wraithlike Walls
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat

claims.claim_text: Date of birth, marital status and religion are conventionally left off an engineering resume.
claims.quote_verbatim: There are bad things to put on your resume. And that is one of them. That and, you know, like your favorite color and, you know, if you're married and your religion.
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: Tailoring a resume to a specific role means restructuring it so the skill the employer is hiring for, such as a particular microcontroller family, is its focus rather than one entry among many; a deliberately neutral format is the alternative when the target role is unknown.
claims.quote_verbatim: Even though he already had it in his resume, they wanted him to change it so it was the focus of the resume.
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: One hiring engineer ranked evidence that a candidate does electronics work outside paid hours as the strongest single positive signal on a resume.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you seem keen and enthusiastic, i.e. you work on shit outside of hours
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: The only function of a resume is to obtain an interview; hiring decisions are made at the interview stage rather than from the document.
claims.quote_verbatim: the sole goal of a resume is to get you in for the interview. That's it. People don't hire based on the resume.
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: An engineer's first position, often an internship or co-op, fixes the application domain recorded on the resume, and later applications tend to stay in that domain because prior experience in it is what employers screen for.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's what you have on your resume. So when, so what job do you try and get next? Well, you've already got experience in that.
claims.episode_title: PCBs, Tektronix & Ham Radio - Habitual Handicraft Hangups

claims.claim_text: Interviewers verify resume claims with deliberately elementary fundamentals questions, such as a simple op-amp circuit or naming three types of analog-to-digital converter, because candidates with impressive resumes routinely fail them.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've had so many good resumes, like very impressive resumes. I come in, and I'll ask them that simple question anyway.
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: A fully public project portfolio can count against a candidate targeting defence or security-cleared work; open-source and past project material can still be shown selectively rather than exposing everything.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you really want to work on like high tech military stuff, sometimes that is dicey
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: Conventional expectations such as dress, spelling and formatting are best simply met rather than used to differentiate, so that the candidate's distinguishing evidence is technical work; standing out on those conventional items forces extra effort later to recover.
claims.quote_verbatim: you should just normalize on the stupid things like the suit and the well-spell-checked resume and stuff like that. And then you shine on the technical stuff.
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Resume presentation matters more than interview attire, because rejection happens at the resume stage whereas reaching the interview already implies the resume passed.
claims.quote_verbatim: having a good looking resume is, you know, and a nicely prepared resume and application is better, is much more valuable than turned up in the suit
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Resume readers give an individual document on the order of seconds on the first pass.
claims.quote_verbatim: You have, like, three seconds, maybe, with most readers of resumes.
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Screening loads of roughly a hundred resumes per opening are routine, and one advertised engineering position drew 29 local applicants alone; interviewing every applicant properly would have taken weeks of full-time work, so the field is cut on the resumes.
claims.quote_verbatim: It'd take me a couple of weeks full-time to interview, to give a fair interview, fair time, to all 29 local applicants.
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: A hiring manager typically shortlists five or six candidates for interview from the whole applicant pool, and the resume is the only evidence available for that cut.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got to pick five or six that I want to interview, you know? So I'm sorry, the resume is the only thing I've got to go on.
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: For an obvious standout candidate, resume defects such as spelling mistakes are overlooked; for borderline candidates competing for a small number of interview slots, presentation quality decides which one is called.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've got a crappy-looking resume and somebody else who I might give the same, you know, have the same inkling for, then I'm sorry, but you're going to miss out
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Screening a field of about thirty student applicants, one hiring engineer weighted side projects above grades and placed candidates with no projects or outside technical interests at the bottom of the list.
claims.quote_verbatim: You, you haven't done any projects at all on the side. You've got no interest outside. Well, okay. Sorry. You go to the bottom of the list
claims.episode_title: Supply Chain Woes And Wares - Nonplussed Neotechnic Nithing

claims.claim_text: According to an instructor who places graduate students with hiring companies, a named online course on a resume, such as an edX electromagnetics course, is weighted comparably to the equivalent classroom course; either serves to get an interview rather than to get the job.
claims.quote_verbatim: when a hiring company, a hiring manager looks at a resume, looking at what courses have they taken, either at school or at a MOOC, they're equally important
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin

claims.claim_text: Resumes from unsuccessful applicants are commonly retained and are the first place a hiring manager looks when a later opening appears.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've kept their resumes because you know I might need somebody else for something right so you know the first port of call I'm going to go back to if I need someone for something else I'm going to go back to those resumes

claims.claim_text: Automated application screening rejects candidates on mechanical criteria such as a keyword-match percentage, which spelling variants like 'colour' versus 'color' can move, and fixed grade-point cutoffs, usually with no human review and no feedback to the applicant.
claims.quote_verbatim: the keyword match is now not 95% it's 92% and you don't meet our cutoff

claims.claim_text: At many university career fairs the company representatives collect resumes but direct every applicant to the online system regardless, so the fair functions largely as advertising.
claims.quote_verbatim: they take your resume you're like so what's going on with my resume here like oh yeah you have to go apply online

claims.claim_text: Some career-fair representatives are engineers who will actually be hiring; presenting a physical board or a photograph of a build rather than only a resume is what makes a candidate memorable afterwards.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you walk up and you don't hand them a resume you hand them a board you've worked on or you just have it with you and like hey can I show you this thing

claims.claim_text: A resume entry that points to documentation of a specific build, such as a blog write-up or a project page on a site like Hackaday, is followed up by reviewers because it makes the claim checkable.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you hand someone a resume and it says I documented this whole build on you know my blog or on the Hackaday project site or somewhere else then you know like that then they'll go and actually look at that

claims.claim_text: On an industry engineering resume, qualifications and publications are placed at the bottom and work experience leads, the reverse of academic convention where publication, patent and funding counts lead.
claims.quote_verbatim: in practical engineering jobs, you know, your qualifications almost don't matter. So, like, they go down the bottom of your resume, your publications go down the bottom, and your work experience is everything

claims.claim_text: A self-taught practitioner entering electronics should describe themselves on a resume by the work they actually perform, for example electronics designer, rather than a prior trade label, provided the claim can be substantiated; in some jurisdictions the title engineer is regulated and cannot be self-applied.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm not saying lie on your resume. No, no. Of course not. You've got to be able to back it up, right?

claims.claim_text: A short contract engagement of a few months, doing troubleshooting or a small design, supplies the first verifiable line of industry experience for a candidate without a formal qualification.
claims.quote_verbatim: Like some little, you know, three-month contract or something, they want you to do something.

claims.claim_text: Referral hiring runs through a small trusted set: practitioners route work to a few people they personally know, because a referral places the referrer's own reputation at risk.
claims.quote_verbatim: in my experience, at least when I refer people, I have a couple friends that I refer all the work that I know of too, right? Because, you know, it's people that I know and I trust them and they're not going to let me down and make me look bad too.

claims.claim_text: Tenures of two to three years per employer read as normal on an engineering resume, while repeatedly moving inside a year reads as a negative signal.
claims.quote_verbatim: two or three years looks decent on your resume

claims.claim_text: A thoroughly documented project write-up covering board layout, stencils, extensive photographs and spectrum and bandwidth measurements is treated as unfakeable evidence of ability, and one such project can be enough on its own to prompt an interview.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can't bullshit your way through this stuff. Right? You know, it's like, you know, he's laid out the boards, stencils, extensive photos.

claims.claim_text: A resume and cover letter with no link to actual work prompts the reviewer to ask where the candidate's work can be found; a personal portfolio site is one way to answer that but is not the only one.
claims.quote_verbatim: I saw the resume, I saw the cover letter, all that stuff. But I asked, you know, where's the portfolio? How do I find your actual work?
claims.episode_title: Fake it till you make it

claims.claim_text: An engineer who recruited co-ops and interns treated one known, unusually demanding university course on a resume as sufficient for an immediate interview; courses of that type, such as building a sixteen-bit processor from scratch in Verilog across thirty- to forty-hour assignments, act as pre-verified evidence of capability.
claims.quote_verbatim: if they have that on their resume, that they've taken that course and they've passed it in like Flint, immediate, immediate interview, if not potential job offer
claims.episode_title: Road trip to the deep space network

claims.claim_text: An engineer who never completed his bachelor's degree reported that a project portfolio published as a web page with downloadable source code, alongside a resume posted to a job site, produced immediate offers.
claims.quote_verbatim: it really helped that I had a portfolio of all the, the stuff I did, like in, on a nice webpage, uh, format, uh, nicely with all the source code for download
claims.speaker: Jeroen Domburg

claims.claim_text: Taking on a project purely to add a named technology to a resume is a recognised failure mode when the candidate has no route to the time and resources needed to become familiar with that technology.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want, uh, people to, uh, to take on projects. They're not actually qualified to do just because they say, oh, they want technology XY in the resume

claims.claim_text: Experience with a free or open-source equivalent of a professional tool is listable on a resume without having taken a design to silicon or production, but an employer standardised on a specific commercial tool may still screen the candidate out.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you try to go to TI and be like, well, I learned on electric, right? This open source chip design program. They're like, well, we use Cadence, so see you later.
claims.episode_title: FPGAs, Robots & Thermocouples - Wampum's Wavering Worth

claims.claim_text: Self-directed product work can be presented under work experience as a named venture rather than as a hobby entry, without misstating what was built.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think it's better to make up a name for your company and then say you're building it for your company and then listed under work experience.

claims.claim_text: Personal projects belong on the resume with direct links to where each one is documented rather than being described in words alone; candidates commonly omit them on the assumption that they do not count.
claims.quote_verbatim: where are all your projects? Like, he's like, Oh, I don't think I should put those on. I'm like, no, you should definitely, definitely put those on there. And, and links, links to your website, where they are focused

claims.claim_text: Resume length is conventionally held to one or two pages, with one page preferred for an early-career candidate.
claims.quote_verbatim: keeping your resume to like one or two sheets tops

claims.claim_text: Photographs of built hardware make a resume visually distinct in a stack of a hundred text-only documents and are what a fatigued reviewer remembers.
claims.quote_verbatim: And you see all the photos and you're, Holy shit. It's something different. So you're going to be looking at the photos, you know, cause it's visually stimulating and you're just going to remember that person.

claims.claim_text: University career-services guidance is built around the intake templates of the large employers that recruit on campus, which suits those employers' HR screens and is less applicable to applications made outside them.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you go to like a career services office and things like that, they're going to be like, here's how you fit into this box that IBM asked for

claims.claim_text: Even employers that publicly de-emphasise formal qualifications still route applications through an HR screen, so a resume must satisfy that screen's checklist before an engineer ever reads it.
claims.quote_verbatim: even those companies, you still have to get through HR. Right. So you've got to have whatever they're looking for.

claims.claim_text: Where limited space forces a choice, an additional technical project entry displaces unrelated general work experience on an engineering resume.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have to choose between putting another project line on your resume and your Dairy Queen experience, put the project line

claims.claim_text: A hiring engineer reported that broad skill claims such as experience in ARM carry little information, implying only that the candidate could work it out given time, whereas naming a specific part family and tool chain such as the STM32 F0 or L0 series and what was completed with it reads as an immediately usable skill.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got experience in arm. Right. They try and like, it's like, yeah, that's pretty broad brush. That's pretty like, yeah, that's not really a useful skill in its own right.

claims.claim_text: Automated application filters reject candidates whom the hiring team has explicitly said it wants to talk to, on mechanical grounds such as an unchecked form field and with no notification; human screening of a hundred-resume stack in an hour likewise both loses good candidates and admits poor-fit ones.
claims.quote_verbatim: because of a filter system on LinkedIn, he didn't click the right button and he just got immediately rejected
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Where a role is attached to a multi-year project, a hiring manager reads a consistent two-year job-change pattern on a resume as predicting the candidate will leave before the project finishes.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I look at a resume and they've moved every two years, then I know that's pretty consistent pattern

claims.claim_text: A job held for less than a year is conventionally omitted from a resume unless the departure had an external cause such as redundancy or the company folding, in which case the reason is stated up front.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've got a job that's like less than a year that you spend at, don't put it on your resume. Like, unless it's like, you know, like you got retrenched or something like that. And you can put the reason right up the top.

attribution_notes: Bundle-wide: speaker labels in this bundle are demonstrably unreliable beyond the five passages flagged attribution_reliable=false. Several adjacent passages (e.g. ep230 [45]/[46], ep496 [78]/[79], ep530 [81]/[82]) carry overlapping text under opposite speaker names, so a name cannot be trusted from the label alone. Where identity was not part of the content, the speaker field was omitted entirely.

ep66: retained the name Dave Jones. Content-confirmed - the passage contrasts IEEE journals with Silicon Chip, an Australian hobbyist magazine, and speaks from the position of an Australian engineer reading resumes.

ep115: retained Greg Charvat for the 'send pictures of boards, not a resume' claim. Content-confirmed - the speaker is the interviewee soliciting applicants for his own group and giving out his own email address. The paired passage [12] labelled Dave Jones contains the same exchange and was not used.

ep124: the whole resume discussion is a two-host exchange in which the labels alternate mid-turn. Names dropped on all five claims taken from this episode, including the 'work outside hours', 'career engineer' and 'money you save the company' judgments; each is recorded as an unnamed hiring practitioner's judgment.

ep230: passages [44]/[45]/[46]/[47]/[48] overlap and the labels contradict each other across the join; the hiring-manager voice (29 local applicants, half a foot of resumes) is one person throughout but cannot be safely named. Names dropped.

ep252: passage flagged ATTRIB-UNRELIABLE. Retained Eric Bogatin by content - the speaker describes running his own certification course, working with graduate students looking for jobs, and talking to companies hiring them, which identifies the interviewee beyond doubt.
ep262: the career-fair passages [56]/[57]/[58] mix a US job-seeker's account with an Australian trade-show account inside single passages; names dropped on all three.
ep288: the call-in answer about a career changer without a degree is a two-voice exchange with no reliable split; names dropped on all three claims taken from it.

ep359: passage labelled Dave Jones, but the content is unambiguously the interviewee - 'I never got my bachelor's', the portfolio webpage, and taking a job at a 25-person broadcasting equipment manufacturer. Attributed to Jeroen Domburg (Sprite_tm), the named guest of that episode.
ep374: passage flagged ATTRIB-UNRELIABLE and labelled Claire Wolf; the turn boundaries inside it are visibly broken, so the name was dropped and the claim left unattributed.

ep496 and ep530: overlapping passage pairs under opposite names (Australian graduation/qualifications material and US resume-review material are interleaved). Names dropped on all claims from both episodes.
ep601: retained Dave Young, the named guest, for the LinkedIn filter account; content-consistent with the guest describing introducing someone to a company he consults for.
ep615: hiring-manager voice discussing a five-year project; the label is Dave Jones on all three passages but the exchange alternates, so the name was dropped.
